injustice.label: Injustice
injustice.insight: Injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no barrier between the supplication of the wronged and Allah. The Quran gives the wronged two options, both legitimate: claiming one's right (“whoever avenges himself after having been wronged — those have not upon them any cause for blame”), or forgiveness and patience (“whoever is patient and forgives — indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination”). And it reassures him: “And never think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do.” The Prophet ﷺ was patient at al-Ta'if, forgave at the conquest of Makkah, and showed no favouritism even in the case of Fatimah had she stolen.

now: Do not answer injustice with injustice; pray: “Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs”
Document precisely what happened
week: Decide: in your case, is claiming your right or forgiving the better course?
Take the lawful routes (dialogue, a mediator, a formal complaint, the courts)
long: Do not let the injustice define who you are or steal your life
Be a support for others who are wronged

questions: What exactly is the right I want?
Is claiming it possible and worth the effort, or is forgiving better for me?
avoid: Taking justice into your own hands outside the law
Staying silent about an injustice that could be removed
injustice.help: For legal matters and questions of rights, consult a lawyer or a specialised body.

insult.label: Insults and mockery
insult.insight: The Quran forbids ridicule, defamation and insulting nicknames, and teaches the believer to answer the ignorant with “peace” — words that keep him free of sin, not words of weakness. The Prophet ﷺ answered “As-samu ‘alaykum” with “And upon you,” without any obscenity, and smiled at the bedouin who pulled him violently. And Allah said to him: “And We already know that your breast is constrained by what they say. So exalt with praise of your Lord.” Your dignity is not in the hands of the one who insults you.

now: Do not reply with an insult; if you want to respond, use a short, measured sentence
Walk away from the situation if it is escalating
week: Set clear boundaries: “I do not accept being spoken to like this”
If it keeps happening (bullying at work or school), report it to those responsible
long: Build your self-confidence on your worth before Allah
Move away from environments that constantly belittle you

questions: Was the insult intended, or is it just a coarse manner?
Which response will I be proud of in a year's time?
avoid: Bottling up the hurt until it explodes

oppressor_power.label: Dealing with an unjust person in authority
oppressor_power.insight: Musa was commanded to speak gently to Pharaoh, yet he did not give up the truth. The believer speaks the word of truth and then says: “And I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of His servants.” Pharaoh's wife prayed to be saved from an environment of oppression: “and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds.” And the Prophet ﷺ taught: “Know that if the nation gathered together to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with what Allah had already written against you.”

now: Do not confront in anger; choose the time and the manner
Say: “Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs”
week: Document the abuses
Look for allies and official channels to complain
long: If the environment is permanently harmful, plan your way out of it

questions: What cards of strength do I hold?
What is the real cost of staying compared with leaving?
avoid: Submitting to an injustice that could be pushed back

honesty.label: Truthfulness and lying
honesty.insight: “Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness… and beware of lying.” Truthfulness brings tranquillity and lying brings doubt. Ka‘b ibn Malik told the Prophet ﷺ the truth and Allah accepted his repentance, while the hypocrites made false excuses — their outward words were accepted and they were left to Allah. Islam keeps a balance: it allows untruth to reconcile people, and between spouses in affectionate words, but the rule is truthfulness.

now: Stop adding a new lie to cover the old one
Think: what is the worst that will happen if I tell the truth?
week: Admit the mistake to whoever deserves to know, choosing the right time and way
Make a rule: I do not promise what I cannot do
long: Make truthfulness part of who you are; it “leads to righteousness”

questions: What am I protecting by lying?
Will frankness here set things right, or just hurt for no benefit?

trust_amanah.label: Trustworthiness, secrets and promises
trust_amanah.insight: “Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due,” and “the signs of a hypocrite are three: whenever he speaks, he lies; whenever he promises, he breaks it; and whenever he is entrusted, he betrays.” Anas kept the Prophet's ﷺ secret even from his own mother. And the one who is consulted is in a position of trust.

now: If you have been trusted with a secret, do not reveal it, even to those closest to you
week: Review your outstanding promises, and keep them or apologise
long: Do not promise anything except what you are able to do

questions: Am I as trustworthy as I expect others to be?
avoid: Revealing secrets in a moment of anger

argument.label: Arguments and heated debate
argument.insight: “I guarantee a house on the outskirts of Paradise for whoever gives up arguing, even if he is in the right.” The Quran commands speaking and debating “in a way that is best,” because “Satan induces dissension among them.” And arrogance is “rejecting the truth” — refusing it after it has become clear.

now: Ask yourself: do I want the truth, or to win?
Lower your voice (“and lower your voice”)
week: Listen to understand, not to reply
If the discussion is going nowhere, end it kindly
long: Accept that people will disagree with you without it turning into hostility

questions: What do I lose if I drop the argument?
Is there a chance that I am the one who is wrong?

arrogance.label: Arrogance and looking down on others
arrogance.insight: “No one who has an atom's weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Paradise… Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.” Humility brings elevation: “No one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him.” The Prophet ﷺ served his family and milked his own sheep, and he told Abu Dharr when he taunted a man: “You are a man who still has some traits of the days of ignorance.”

now: If you have wronged someone, apologise to them
week: Serve someone else in something simple
Listen to someone who ranks below you
long: Watch your reaction when you are criticised

questions: When did I last admit that I was wrong?
avoid: Looking down on people because of money, origin or education

different_belief.label: Religious differences in the family and society
different_belief.insight: “Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills” was revealed about the Prophet's ﷺ own uncle: guidance is in Allah's hands, and your role is “So remind, you are only a reminder; you are not over them a controller.” The way is wisdom, good counsel and discussion in the best manner, gentle speech, keeping kindness and family ties (“keep ties with your mother”), and being good to those who live in peace with you (“that you be righteous toward them and act justly toward them”).

now: Do not turn every meeting into a sermon
Be an example in conduct before words
week: Choose a calm moment for a short, gentle conversation
Pray for their guidance in your prostration
long: Protect the relationship; it is the bridge that goodness travels across
Do not despair and do not be impatient

questions: Do they see in my behaviour something that attracts them, or something that repels them?

charity.label: Giving and helping others
charity.insight: “The most beloved of people to Allah are those most beneficial to people,” and “whoever relieves a believer of a hardship, Allah will relieve him of a hardship of the Day of Resurrection.” Giving does not require money: “a good word is charity,” and “your smiling in your brother's face is charity.” And the one who looks after an orphan will be with the Prophet ﷺ in Paradise.

now: Do one kind deed today, even a small one
week: Set aside a fixed amount for charity, even a little
long: Take on a regular volunteering role

questions: What talent do I have that I could use to benefit people?
avoid: Reminding people of your favours, or hurting them

ungrateful.label: Ingratitude
ungrateful.insight: Whoever works for Allah's sake is not crushed when he is not thanked: “We feed you only for the countenance of Allah. We wish not from you reward or gratitude.” And to the one who keeps ties with relatives who cut him off: “You will continue to have a supporter from Allah against them.” Abu Bakr resumed spending on Mistah after his offence. Yet at the same time, “he who does not thank people does not thank Allah” — gratitude is a right, and gently reminding of it is legitimate.

now: Renew your intention: for whom was I giving?
Allow yourself to feel let down without letting it turn into bitterness
week: Calmly express your need for appreciation to those who matter to you
Balance your giving: do not give what drains you
long: Keep doing good and keep your reward with Allah

questions: Was I expecting something in return?
Am I giving in a way that drains me?
avoid: Reminding people of what you gave
Stopping all good because of one person
triggers: they only call when they need

decision.label: Hard decisions and indecision
decision.insight: The Prophetic way of deciding: consultation (“and consult them in the matter”; “the one consulted is in a position of trust”), istikharah (the Prophet ﷺ taught it to his Companions as he taught them a surah of the Quran), then resolve and trust (“and when you have decided, then rely upon Allah”), then contentment with the outcome and leaving “if only”. At al-Hudaybiyah the Prophet ﷺ accepted terms that seemed harsh, with far-sighted vision, and they turned out to be an opening.

now: Write down the options, and for each: the gains, the risks, and what pleases Allah
Pray the istikharah prayer
week: Consult two people: one an expert in the subject, the other someone who knows you well
Gather the missing information
long: After deciding: rely on Allah and go ahead, and do not live in “if only”

questions: Which option would I regret not trying in ten years' time?
What pleases Allah in this choice?
Am I waiting for a certainty that will never come?
avoid: Deciding in a moment of strong emotion
Blaming istikharah if the outcome is not what you wanted
triggers: do not know what to do

animals.label: Mercy to animals
animals.insight: A man entered Paradise because of a dog he gave water to, and a woman entered the Fire because of a cat she locked up. And “Allah has prescribed excellence in everything.”

now: Be kind to the animal in front of you
week: If you see an animal being harmed, advise gently
long: Make mercy to creatures a habit
